Harbour District plan › notes › kit
- Kit adopt / reject (brief 007 A replaces the 006 B note; 007 lifts 'the kit fits the plan, never the other way' for the skyline).
- ADOPT SpaceHQ: signatures.space-hq, the dominant icon at Crown Circus east, 252 m; regen SpaceHQ_Portal (terminal drum r 40 to 34 with S1 and Crown Circus station inside; shaft −29 m, tip kept).
- ADOPT Tower_Starburst: towers.sites avenue-starburst, the tallest rival, tiers cut to the 3.6 grid, tip 194.3.
- ADOPT Tower_Needle: towers.sites avenue-needle, saucer floor to storey 30 (100.8 over the deck), tip 167.8.
- ADOPT DiscTower ×2: towers.sites avenue-gate-w / -e, 88 m apart across Crown Avenue, shaft to the grid (111.6), tip 165.6.
- ADOPT SkyBridge: towers.skyBridges avenue-gate, as built (70 m clear between the DiscTowers), floor 67.03.
- ADOPT Tower_Terrace: towers.sites crescent-terrace, terraces to the grid, tip 122.7.
- ADOPT Skylon: landmarks.skylon in Starline Green, × 0.925, top 100.
- ADOPT LinerDock: landmarks.liner-berth, a caisson 20 m off the Market Docks crane walk; regen at × 0.5 (tip 102.6 ≤ 104) so the Skyport Tower stays the harbour's icon; caisson only until then.
- ADOPT SkyRailStation_Twin (Vela, brief 007 C): the four S1 stations; inside SpaceHQ and the Skyport Tower as platform decks only.
- KEEP SphereStation (landmarks.sphere × 0.425), Skyport_Tower_Portal (skyport-tower), CircusMonument, ParabolicArch (skyport-tower.gateway), SkyPad_Roof (pad, hover-pad roofs).
- KEEP the 006 B regen sites: parade-gate-n / -s Tower_Stepped, harbour-hotel Tower_Saucer, crescent-tower Tower_Atom, lantern-beacon Tower_Lantern.
- REJECT Tower_Setback (172 m, 30 m plan): no crown of its own, and grammar §6 already crowns every ≥ 9-storey block; a sixth rival would crowd the cluster under rivalMax.
- REJECT SkyRailStation (single beam, rail top 22, 40 m platforms): superseded by SkyRailStation_Twin.
- Rule changes these sites need (signature ground, portals, skyline, platform clearance) are handed to Splice: see the brief 007 A report.

hits.text:
Harbour District plan › notes › concept
- Buchanan's hierarchy: a primary ring (Sunset Way, Crown Road, Harbour Road, Comet Row) carries through traffic round the district; district distributors (the Boulevard, Market Street, Circus Road, Crown Avenue) feed it; access roads serve seven environmental areas and never link two distributors.
- Every way a car can enter an environmental area is a gate. For a mission, the gates are the seal points; the Records Precinct has two.
- Crown Circus is the hub (EPCOT 1966: a radial centre with transit through it). Four arms: the Boulevard south, Crown Avenue north, Circus Road west, Crown Parade (a pedestrian mall) east to the harbour.
- Tram T1 runs in the Boulevard's central reservation with stops about 300 m apart. It turns on a balloon loop round the circus island (R 28), so single-ended trams need no crossover. South of Comet Row it runs on to Southside.
- Sky rail S1 is the airport line (Tokyo 1964). One straight trunk: Skyport, Harbour, Crown Circus, Sphere Gardens, then the West End. It runs over public space: Circus Road's median, the circus island, the Parade and the Skyport Pier, and since brief 007 it threads the buildings over them: through the SpaceHQ drum (Crown Circus station inside), over the open Parade (the Galleries' side galleries under glazed barrel canopies, the Parade itself open to the sky; the beam on its mall pylons), through the Parade Gate block and the Skyport Tower's portal (Skyport station inside). Trains turn on a loop over the water round the skyport pad; the Skyport station stands on the pier's apron, the landside end.
- The two systems cross at right angles at Crown Circus, the one interchange (sky station to tram stop ≈ 120 m).
- The Records Axis: the Sphere Gardens sky station, Garden Walk, the café, the fountain, the raised table on Orbit Walk and the office door all sit on x = −160.
- Players cross any road anywhere. Kerbs, medians, the tram reservation and the circus are walkable ground (no guard rails); crossings and raised tables only calm traffic. Walking distances on this sheet are measured that way: round buildings and water, straight over streets.
